svg.title: CPextractor: Automated Literature Mining for Crystal Plasticity Parameters
svg.desc: A0 landscape academic poster describing the CPextractor pipeline, schema design, table extraction challenges, evaluation strategy, representative case-study results, and take-home message.

g.text: CPextractor: Automated Literature Mining for Crystal Plasticity Parameters
Structured extraction, normalization, evidence grounding, and dataset construction from scientific papers
[Institution] | Literature-to-database workflow for trustworthy CP parameter curation
Parse -> extract -> normalize -> audit -> ingest -> retrieve
Real schema objects: materials, conditions, models, evidence_objects, parameter_claims
Why CP parameter curation does not scale manually
Parameters are distributed across prose, tables, references, and supplements.
Table content may be image-backed, irregular, or split across multi-row headers.
Names, symbols, units, provenance, and applicability vary by paper and model scope.
Flat extraction is not enough for reuse, auditing, or database ingest.
CPextractor addresses this as an evidence-grounded curation workflow, not a single extraction step.
Implemented pipeline from full text to trusted database records
The project runtime follows the repo workflow: parse Elsevier XML, run two-stage LLM extraction, normalize scope, ground evidence, evaluate with a committee, and build database-ready claims.

Confidence fusion produces parameter-level and document-level quality signals, then the pipeline builds `parameter_claims` and the finalized hierarchy for downstream DB ingest, retrieval, review, and analytics.
Hierarchical objects encode scientific scope, not just fields
Design principle: keep material identity, process state, condition, model, provenance, and evidence separable.
From difficult tables to grounded claims
The pipeline resolves row and column semantics, normalizes units and scope, and links the final claim back to table snippets, file spans, and reusable `evidence_objects`.
Multi-level quality assessment with a real case-study example

Benchmark design in code covers extraction correctness, judge correctness and calibration, and database utility. The values above come from the opened Acta Materialia case study; replace with corpus-level results for the final poster.
Corpus-level results from 288 real full-text papers
Raw extraction maximizes recall. Claim normalization can split one raw row into multiple scoped claims.
Converts unstructured CP literature into structured, validated, evidence-grounded knowledge.
Preserves provenance, scope, and uncertainty so extracted parameters remain scientifically reusable.
Creates dataset infrastructure for reproducible constitutive modeling, retrieval, and analytics.

Database tables, review queue, evidence-grounded RAG, parameter analytics, and reusable structured datasets.
